\begin{abstract}
Cost Per Task (benchmark-cost-per-task) is a public npm benchmark package in the benchmark-* family, version 0.2.0, status alpha. This report records what the package measures in its own words, its deterministic grader and its SDK, CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces, and the offline validation the family data holds: a scripted good policy mean of 1 and a scripted bad policy mean of 0 over 30 tasks, from mock runs at seeds 1 and 2 on the public task split generated with seed 20261015. The review record shows 2 fix rounds, 1 defect classes with public locators, and 6 merged feature pull requests of which 5 were approved. The best trivial policy scored 0.0000 at both versions. No real-model scores are reported. Software concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422371, family paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428802.
\end{abstract}
\section{What the package asks}

benchmark-cost-per-task is an open-source AI agent benchmark for
dollars per verified back-office task. It measures successful work,
retries, turns, and tokens. Deterministic simulators check every
result.

\section{Grader and surfaces}
The grading document states the mechanism in its own words:
% quote: benchmark-cost-per-task/docs/grading.md#L3
\begin{quote}
Every task starts a fresh virtual file system and CRM. The grader
replays the submitted tool log against that initial state; it never
trusts a submitted \texttt{finalState} or tool result. A task scores 1
only when all files and CRM records exactly match the task's expected
state and \texttt{finish\_task} was called. Otherwise it scores 0 with
the mismatched state named in the reason.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-cost-per-task/blob/v0.2.0/docs/grading.md#L3}{\texttt{benchmark-cost-per-task:docs/grading.md\#L3}}.}

The index entry summarises the grader as: ``Deterministic replay followed by exact virtual file-system and CRM state verification.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-cost-per-task.grader}).

\section{Offline validation}
No real model was run. The family data records mock runs at seeds \pkgMockSeedA{} and \pkgMockSeedB{}
over the public task split generated with seed \pkgPublicSeed{}, on version \pkgVersion{}:
the scripted good policy reaches a mean of \pkgGoodMean{} (weakest task \pkgGoodMin{}),
the scripted bad policy a mean of \pkgBadMean{} (best task \pkgBadMax{}),
and the run at mock seed \pkgMockSeedA{} scores \pkgMockMean{} over \pkgTaskCount{} tasks
with a bootstrap interval of \pkgMockCiLow{} to \pkgMockCiHigh{} (\pkgMockPassed{} tasks passed; cost \$\pkgMockCost{}).
Source: \texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, collected by \texttt{scripts/collect.mjs}.
The README prints a sample run:

\section{Preregistered trivial-policy check}
The check design is described in the family paper: trivial policies ran each package in the registered set
at \pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{} through a local fake model server answering through
the package's own OpenAI provider (\texttt{paper/sections/prereg.tex}).
The preregistered check ran \pkgTrivialPolicies{} generic trivial policies against this package at versions
\pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{}. The best trivial score was \pkgTrivialOld{} at \pkgTrivialVerOld{}
and \pkgTrivialNew{} at \pkgTrivialVerNew{}, won by \texttt{\pkgTrivialPolicy{}} (\texttt{paper/data/trivial.csv}).
\section{Limitations and what is not claimed}
The package documents its own limit:
% quote: benchmark-cost-per-task/README.md#L185
\begin{quote}
Public tasks and expected states can enter training data.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-cost-per-task/blob/v0.2.0/README.md#L185}{\texttt{benchmark-cost-per-task:README.md\#L185}}.}

This report claims no model capability: it records no real-model run, no leaderboard, and no comparison between models.
These offline numbers describe the graders and the scripted policies. They say nothing about a hosted model.
Package status is \texttt{\pkgStatus{}}; saturation is \texttt{\pkgSaturation{}} (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}).
Disclosure: the package was built by AI coding agents in sessions the author configured, the reviews cited here
are agent reviews, and this report was generated by \texttt{scripts/pkg-reports.mjs} on \pkgSnapshotDate{} from the cached sources named above.
